english.title: Use in navigation an unsafe lighter / barge / vessel likely to endanger human life
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[used]_
(B)_[caused to be used]_
(C)_[permitted to be used]_

in navigation a

(D)_[lighter]_
(E)_[barge]_
(F)_[vessel, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF VESSEL,]_

when, because of

(G)_[the defective condition of its hull,]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 99 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.

date and location

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Proceedings under section 99 of the Merchant Shipping Act may not be instituted except by or with the consent of the Secretary of State.
(ii) This section does not affect the liability of the owners of any lighter, barge or like vessel in respect of loss of life or personal injury caused to any person carried in the vessel - section 99(3)

other.penalty:
Summary: Afine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limitfor prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
